02 / THE SCIENTIFIC FOUNDATION

Before the benchmark,
there was the physics.

How does stochastic scattering change the WIMPs that reach an underground detector? The original project follows particles through atmosphere and crust, then scores xenon nuclear recoils.

01

A halo, not a single speed.

A truncated Maxwellian velocity distribution is shifted into the laboratory frame. Incident flux sets the normalization.

02

Each collision changes the path.

Layered atmosphere, mixed crust, elastic spin-independent scattering and a Helm form factor connect transport to recoil response.

03

Score the detector response.

Compare collisionless, ballistic and full transport at an idealized xenon scoring plane. Track uncertainty across initial histories.

A concrete source, with explicit limits.

100 GeV/c² WIMPs · 1 km depth · 5,000 histories per cross section. Infinite planar geometry, illustrative compositions, ideal threshold. No experimental discovery or exclusion is claimed.

Read the original scientific report ↗
REAL PHYSICS PROJECT→FRAGILE REASONING POINTS→4 SYNTHETIC TASKS→FROZEN REFERENCES→TRANSCRIPT REPLAY

W_transport and W_geometry isolate source-inspired transport and scoring issues. R_calibration and R_search extend the reliability question into fully specified synthetic resonant-cavity analysis; they are not derived WIMP predictions or real cavity measurements.

WHAT THIS DOES AND DOES NOT ESTABLISH
These records document reproducible discrepancies on four narrow synthetic tasks. They do not estimate a general AI failure rate, validate an underground detector, or establish a physical signal. R_search is a positive structured control within the stated tolerance; its small numerical discrepancies are still visible. Record hashes are integrity checks, not independent provider authentication.
